To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
F420H _{2} -dependent reductases can catalyze the enantio-, chemoselective and regioselectively ene-reducing of α,β unsaturated ketones and α,β unsatured aldehydes.
F420H _{2} -driven enzymes are able to reduce α,β- and γ,δ- unsaturated aldehydes with very high enantioselectivities, regioselectivities, chemoselectivities, and conversions.
F420H _{2} -dependent enzymes can perform highly selective ene-reducing biotransformations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel biocatalysts and their application in asymmetric synthesis.
the identification of new biocatalysts, which are able to perform ene-reducing reactions with high regio- and enantioselectivities.
the development of a new biocatalytic platform for the reduction of unsaturated carbonyl compounds, which can be used for the synthesis of chiral building blocks and natural products.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

F420H _{2} -dependent enzymes display a reversed stereopreference compared to their FMN-dependent counterparts, which makes them a valuable alternative for the ene-reduction of α,β -unsaturated ketones or aldehydes.
the use of F420H2 reductases for the reduction of enones is an attractive and promising alternative to the use of OYEs.
F420H 2 -driven ene-reduction biocatalysis is an emerging and highly promising field.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a new class of ene-reductases that are capable to perform the same reactions as OYEs with a different enantio- and chemodivergent outcome.
we have demonstrated that both F420H2- and NADH-driven enzymes can be used for ene-reduces with excellent selectivity and conversions.
FDRs are complementary biocatalysts to OYEs for ene-reducing biotransformations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
F420H 2-driven reductase-catalyzed ene-reduction reactions can provide a complementary and orthogonal approach to FMN-dependent OYE-catalyzed reductions.
F420-dependent enzymes can be used to perform highly selective reductions that are not possible with the FMN-dependent reductases.
F420H _{2} -driven enzymes can be used to reduce α,β- unsaturated ketones and can be used as a complementary tool for the synthesis of enantiomerically pure compounds.
